intended_object: The basis-modification map δ from the Demushkin-group classification: for a free pro-p group F on a finite set and m ≥ 1, the F_p-bilinear map gr_1(F) × gr_m(F)^X → gr_{m+1}(F), δ_ρ(ω) = Σ c_i(πω_i + C(p,2)[ω_i,ξ_i]) + Σ_{i<k} a_{ik}([ω_i,ξ_k] − [ω_k,ξ_i]), which computes the class of r⁻¹θ_w(r). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body uses `Basis.constr` on the standard basis `degreeOneBasis` of gr_1(F). On a p-power basis vector πξ_i it gives `gradedPow` of v_i plus C(p,2)•[v_i, ξ_i]; on a bracket basis vector [ξ_i, ξ_k] with i<k it gives [v_i, ξ_k] − [v_k, ξ_i]. This is exactly the docstring's formula, and the library proves the basis values and the general expansion (`basisModificationDelta_degreeOneBasis_inl`, `_inr`, `_apply`). The intended meaning is also proved: `gradedDeviation_basisModification` shows the map equals the graded deviation of θ_w, and `gradedMk_inv_mul_basisModification` shows it gives the class of r⁻¹θ_w r in gr_{m+1}. The formula is mathematically sound: C(p,2) vanishes mod p for odd p, and (xw)² ≡ x²w²[w,x] accounts for the extra term when p = 2. The free pro-p group on a finite set is the natural setting for this map in the Demushkin classification. The linear order on X only indexes the basis; the map itself is intrinsic, being the graded deviation. Mathlib has no counterpart.
